title: Microsoft stops insisting you need a "Copilot+ PC"
gist: Microsoft dropped Copilot+ PC branding from its new Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Plus Surface devices despite meeting the spec, reflecting fading consumer interest in 'AI PCs' (Dell also killed its AI laptop branding), Recall security baggage, the RAM shortage, and a shift in marketing focus toward Nvidia's RTX Spark laptop GPUs.

insights.claim: Microsoft's new Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch (2nd Edition), shipping October 13, are not branded Copilot+ PCs even though they meet the requirements, per Surface CVP Brett Ostrum.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Microsoft de-emphasizing its own AI PC label signals the on-device AI upgrade narrative is not driving PC demand.
insights.locator: Speaking with Windows Central, Brett Ostrum

insights.claim: The new Surface devices run Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Plus processors with a Hexagon NPU rated at 80 TOPS, double the 40 TOPS Copilot+ minimum (along with 16GB RAM and 256GB storage).
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Qualcomm keeps Surface design wins, but NPU TOPS is losing marketing value as a differentiator.

insights.claim: Microsoft's Copilot+ PC landing page now redirects to a 'performance PCs' page that mentions the label far less prominently.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Confirms a deliberate marketing pivot away from AI-first PC messaging.

insights.claim: The Copilot+ PC campaign helped push the AI PC idea during a post-COVID PC sales lull, and Satya Nadella said in January 2025 that Copilot+ PCs were 15 percent of US premium laptop sales over the holidays.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: The AI PC label had served its purpose as a refresh catalyst; its retirement suggests that catalyst is spent.
insights.locator: Further, the Copilot+ PC marketing campaign

insights.claim: IDC's Jitesh Ubrani says interest in AI PCs has been wavering because cloud AI is widely available and on-device use cases are limited, and this indifference may benefit PC OEMs by reducing the need to ship large amounts of RAM amid a RAM shortage.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Weak on-device AI demand eases OEM memory cost pressure during the RAM shortage but removes a premium-pricing lever.
insights.quote: General interest in AI PCs has been wavering for a while, since cloud-based options are widely available and the use cases for on-device AI have been limited.

insights.claim: Dell killed the AI laptop branding it introduced in 2025, and its 2026 lineup makes minimal mention of AI PCs.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Industry-wide retreat from AI PC messaging, not just Microsoft.
insights.locator: More evidence of waning AI PC

insights.claim: The Copilot+ PC label was marred by persistent security and privacy concerns around its Recall feature.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Privacy backlash can undermine on-device AI feature adoption.
insights.locator: There are numerous reasons why Microsoft

insights.claim: Microsoft has confirmed a Surface Laptop Ultra with Nvidia's upcoming RTX Spark laptop GPUs this fall, and RTX Spark may take marketing precedence over Copilot+ positioning.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Nvidia gaining premium Windows laptop mindshare could be a competitive threat to Qualcomm's NPU-centric positioning.
